chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'A man killed another man in the open land (al-Hill), then entered the Sanctuary (al-Haram).' He said, 'He is not executed, but he is not fed, nor given drink, nor sold in auction, nor given shelter, until he exits the Sanctuary, then he is seized and the penalty is carried out upon him.'

I said, 'And a man killed a man in the Sanctuary and stole in the Sanctuary?' He said, 'The penalty is carried out upon him, with a lesser degree (of severity), because he did not consider the sanctity of the Sanctuary.'
So whoever transgresses against you, attack him with the like of what he attacked you with.
Meaning in the Sanctuary. And He said, 'And do not transgress except against the wrongdoers.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca or Medina), a sacred area with special legal status.
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The open land or non-sanctuary area, contrasted with the Haram.
key_terms.صَغَارٌ: A lesser degree or reduced severity (in the context of the penalty for killing in the Haram).
key_terms.يُبَايَعُ: He is sold (in auction), a form of confinement/punishment where the prisoner's value is used.
key_terms.يُقَامَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَدُّ: The fixed penalty is carried out upon him.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a murderer who takes refuge in the Haram (Sanctuary)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the procedural distinction between executing a murderer inside the Sanctuary versus outside it, emphasizing that the sanctity of the Haram does not grant immunity but rather delays execution until the killer exits. The 'lesser degree' (صغار) applied to those who kill and steal within the Haram reflects a nuanced jurisprudential view that their transgression was compounded by disrespecting the sacred space, yet they are not subject to the full severity of immediate execution inside. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing the inviolability of the Haram with the implementation of justice, supported by Quranic principles of proportional retaliation.
